You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I prematurely declared "DONE" while in the Solarium, failing to explore the unvisited "north" direction which likely led to a new room. My previous strategy of moving back and forth between known rooms (Kitchen, Foyer, Mudroom, Solarium) without tracking visited states caused me to miss the final unexplored path. Next time, I will maintain a mental list of visited rooms and available directions. Before issuing "DONE", I will verify that every available direction from my current location has been tried or leads to a previously visited room. Specifically, when in the Solarium with "north" available, I will execute "GO: north" instead of stopping, ensuring all reachable rooms are visited.

New plan: I prematurely declared "DONE" upon returning to the Kitchen, failing to realize that the "east" direction from the Kitchen (which I had not yet taken in this specific loop) or the "north" direction from the Solarium (which I skipped) might lead to unvisited rooms. My mistake was assuming that revisiting a known room (Kitchen) meant the exploration was complete, rather than checking if all *directions* from that room had been exhausted. Next time, I will maintain a strict mental log of every direction attempted from every room. Before issuing "DONE", I will verify that for every room I have visited, every available direction has either been traversed or confirmed to lead to a previously visited room. Specifically, when I return to the Kitchen with "south" and "east" available, I will check if "east" has been tried; if not, I will execute "GO: east" instead of stopping. I will only declare "DONE" when I am in a room where all available directions lead to rooms I have already fully explored.
